title: Devcontainer becomes a full builder image with agent hooks
summary: This change turns the devcontainer from a minimal Rust image into a complete builder environment: it pins and installs moon, Node/pnpm, Bun, gh, actionlint, uv, the NVIDIA skill tools, and four coding agents (codex, claude-code, opencode, omp), builds the dsh/omp/opencode writing-check plugins from the workspace lockfile, and wires every agent's hook files root-owned and read-only so `osf hook` runs on prompt and stop. The git wrapper now forces the hooks path per-invocation under /workspace instead of a system-wide core.hooksPath, and a battery of build-time tests proves the wrapper, hooks, toolchain read-only-ness and image cleanliness.

nodes.label: Developer host
nodes.summary: The machine running VS Code and Docker; supplies GH_TOKEN via remoteEnv.

nodes.label: devcontainer.json
nodes.subtitle: workspaceMount + remoteEnv
nodes.summary: Now pins the bind mount to /workspace, forwards GH_TOKEN, and checks osf/moon/node/pnpm in postCreateCommand.

nodes.label: Dockerfile
nodes.subtitle: +493 lines
nodes.summary: The single build recipe: pins every tool by version and SHA-256, installs the agents, builds the plugins, wires hooks, and runs the build-time test scripts.

nodes.label: Pinned toolchain
nodes.subtitle: moon, node, pnpm, bun, gh, actionlint, uv
nodes.summary: Each tool is downloaded from its own release, verified against a published SHA-256, and installed root-owned under /usr/local.

nodes.label: SkillSpector / SkillEvaluator
nodes.subtitle: uv tool install at pinned commits
nodes.summary: Installed via uv from NVIDIA git commits, with UV_TOOL_DIR and UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR moved out of root's home so dev can read them.

nodes.label: Coding agents
nodes.subtitle: codex, claude-code, opencode, omp
nodes.summary: Global npm installs pinned to exact versions; omp additionally needs Bun because its shebang is `#!/usr/bin/env bun`.

nodes.label: dsh
nodes.subtitle: @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.0-rc.2
nodes.summary: Installed from its own lockfile under /opt/dsh and symlinked onto PATH.

nodes.label: Plugin build
nodes.subtitle: pnpm --filter dsh,omp,opencode
nodes.summary: Builds the three writing-check integrations from the workspace pnpm lockfile so their dependency versions match what CI already tests.

nodes.label: Agent hook files
nodes.subtitle: root-owned, mode 0444
nodes.summary: Codex gets /etc/codex; claude-code and opencode get system copies under /etc; omp and dsh keep home-only copies because they have no system-wide path.

nodes.label: dsh profiles
nodes.subtitle: factory + headless
nodes.summary: Both profiles get the osf-dsh-plugin under node_modules and a cordis.patch.yml; only cordis.yml stays dev-owned because dsh rewrites it on start.

nodes.label: git wrapper
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/git
nodes.summary: Refuses --no-verify and -n on commit and --no-verify on push, and now forces core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks on the command line for every git call under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT.

nodes.label: git hooks
nodes.subtitle: pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push
nodes.summary: Root-owned scripts that each call osf; unchanged in content but now reached only through the wrapper's forced hooks path.

nodes.label: osf binary
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/osf
nodes.summary: Built from the workspace and installed read-only; the hook files and git hooks all shell out to it.

nodes.label: Build-time tests
nodes.subtitle: 9 scripts run during docker build
nodes.summary: Each script proves one property of the image (wrapper refusals, hook wiring, toolchain read-only, image cleanliness) and fails the build if it does not hold.

nodes.label: osf-path.sh
nodes.subtitle: /etc/profile.d
nodes.summary: Re-adds osf, cargo and the agent binaries to PATH for login shells, which otherwise reset PATH before reading profile.d.

nodes.label: user dev
nodes.subtitle: no sudo, own CARGO_HOME
nodes.summary: The non-root user the container runs as; owns its home and its cargo cache but nothing under /usr/local or /opt/factory.

nodes.label: /workspace
nodes.subtitle: bind mount of the repo
nodes.summary: The one folder the git wrapper treats as the workspace; devcontainer.json binds the repo here and OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT names the same value.

nodes.label: Agent process
nodes.subtitle: codex / claude / opencode / omp / dsh
nodes.summary: Whichever agent the developer runs; it reads its own hook file and shells out to osf hook on the events it supports.

nodes.label: osf hook
nodes.subtitle: prompt and stop events
nodes.summary: The one command every agent hook file calls; it has no pre-tool-use event, so none is wired.

nodes.label: git
nodes.subtitle: real git, via the wrapper
nodes.summary: Every git invocation under /workspace goes through the wrapper first, which then execs the real git with the forced hooks path.

nodes.label: npm registry
nodes.summary: Source of the agent packages, dsh, and the skills CLI.

nodes.label: GitHub releases
nodes.summary: Source of the pinned tool tarballs, each verified against a published SHA-256.

nodes.label: Model APIs
nodes.summary: The LLM endpoints the agents call; the image ships no credentials for them.

nodes.label: GitHub API
nodes.summary: Reached by gh and by the builder role when opening or checking pull requests.

edges.label: bind mount
edges.summary: devcontainer.json now names the mount target explicitly as /workspace.

edges.label: docker build
edges.summary: The host builds the image from the Dockerfile; the build now runs the test scripts as part of the build.
Each tool is fetched, checksum-verified and installed root-owned.
Global npm installs pinned to exact versions.
npm ci from the dsh lockfile, then symlinked onto PATH.
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile then a filtered build of the three integrations.

edges.label: dist/src
edges.summary: The built plugin is copied into both dsh profiles' node_modules.
Hook files are copied in and locked to root:root 0444.
The wrapper is installed read-only and its refusals are proven at build time.
Each test script runs during the build and fails it on a broken invariant.
osf is still built from the workspace and installed read-only.
uv installs both tools at pinned commits, with their dirs made readable to dev.
The profile.d script restores PATH for login shells.

edges.label: runs as dev
edges.summary: Every agent runs as the non-root dev user, which is why the hook files must be readable and the toolchain read-only.

edges.label: osf hook prompt|stop
edges.summary: The hook files the image installs point every agent at osf hook for the prompt and stop events.
Each agent reads its own root-owned hook file at startup.
dsh reads its profile's cordis.patch.yml and plugin from node_modules.
The developer's git commands resolve to the wrapper on PATH.

edges.label: PATH shim
edges.summary: The wrapper is what /usr/local/bin/git resolves to; it forces the hooks path and then execs the real git.

edges.label: core.hooksPath
edges.summary: The wrapper passes core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks on the command line for every git call under the workspace, replacing the old system-wide setting.
Each hook script shells out to osf for its check.

edges.label: OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT
edges.summary: The wrapper decides whether a repository is under the workspace by comparing against this env var, which the Dockerfile sets from the same build arg devcontainer.json uses.
git-wrapper.sh proves the refusals and the forced hooks path.
agent-hooks.sh proves every enabled agent's hook file is root-owned and read-only and that osf hook answers a sample payload.
toolchain-readonly.sh proves dev cannot write to any root-owned toolchain folder.

edges.label: SHA-256 verified
edges.summary: Every tool tarball comes from a GitHub release and is checked against a published checksum.
Agent packages, dsh and the skills CLI come from npm.
The agents call their model endpoints at runtime; the image ships no credentials.
The builder role uses gh, which reads GH_TOKEN forwarded from the host.

flows.title: An agent prompt reaches osf hook
flows.summary: What happens when a developer submits a prompt to any of the installed agents: the agent reads its root-owned hook file, shells out to osf hook, and the hook runs as the non-root dev user against the workspace.

messages.label: read hook config
messages.note: Codex reads /etc/codex/hooks/osf-prompt.toml; claude-code reads its managed settings; omp and dsh read their home copies.

messages.label: read repo state
messages.note: The hook inspects the repository under the workspace root to decide its answer.

flows.title: A git commit goes through the wrapper
flows.summary: Every git call under /workspace resolves to the wrapper, which refuses the bypass flags, forces the hooks path on the command line, and then execs the real git so the root-owned hooks run.

messages.label: PATH shim
messages.note: /usr/local/bin/git is the wrapper, so this is not an explicit call the developer makes.

messages.label: reject --no-verify / -n
messages.note: The wrapper refuses the bypass flags before doing anything else.

messages.label: core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks
messages.note: Forced on the command line for every call under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT, replacing the old system-wide setting.

views.title: Devcontainer image and runtime
views.summary: The image bakes a root-owned toolchain, the agents, and their hook files; the dev user runs the agents and git against the bind-mounted workspace.

children.title: Hook wiring
children.summary: How each agent's hook file reaches osf hook, and how the git wrapper forces the hooks path instead of relying on a system-wide setting.

children.title: Image build
children.summary: What the Dockerfile fetches, verifies, installs and proves before the image is usable.

views.title: Runtime flows
views.summary: The two ordered sequences this change is really about: an agent prompt reaching osf hook, and a git commit reaching the root-owned hooks.

steps.heading: A much bigger image
steps.body: The Dockerfile grows from a Rust base into a full builder environment.

steps.heading: Plugins built from the lockfile
steps.body: The dsh, omp and opencode integrations are built with the workspace's own pnpm lockfile.

steps.heading: Hooks are root-owned

steps.heading: The wrapper forces the hooks path

steps.body: The agent reads its hook file and shells out to osf hook as the dev user.

steps.heading: A commit reaches the hooks
